claim: circHIPK3 is produced from the second exon of the HIPK3 gene.
source: circHIPK3 is produced from the second exon of the HIPK3 gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In all cell lines except for one, circHIPK3 is higher expressed than the linear transcript.
source: In all cell lines except for one, circHIPK3 is higher expressed than the linear transcript (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The circHIPK3 siRNA did not lead to co-knockdown of the linear HIPK3 mRNA or HIPK3 protein.
source: As expected, the circHIPK3 siRNA did not lead to co-knockdown of the linear HIPK3 mRNA or HIPK3 protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Thousands of genes are differentially expressed upon circHIPK3 KD across time in UMUC3 (n = 3072) and J82 (n = 2389).
source: Next, we performed differential expression analyses and identified thousands of genes that are differentially expressed (DE) upon circHIPK3 KD across time in UMUC3 (n = 3072) and J82 (n = 2389) (false discovery rate [FDR] <0.1, Benjamini–Hochberg correction)
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with specific numbers and statistical criteria.

claim: There is a large overlap (n = 1104) of differentially expressed genes between UMUC3 and J82 cell lines.
source: with a large overlap (n = 1104) between cell lines (p < 2.2e−16, Fisher's exact test, Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 92% of the shared DE genes between UMUC3 and J82 cells show the same perturbation profile in both cell lines.
source: Convincingly, 92% of the shared DE genes between UMUC3 and J82 cells show the same perturbation profile in both cell lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: circHIPK3 contains 11 distinctly conserved miRNA target sites based on AGO-CLIP data.
source: Based on AGO-CLIP data of experimentally defined miRNA-binding sites, we previously identified 11 distinctly conserved miRNA target sites in circHIPK3 (Hamilton et al., 2016; Hamilton et al., 2013; Okholm et al., 2017; Figure 2A and Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Neither the target sites for miR-148-3p nor any of the other circHIPK3-miRNAs are enriched among downregulated genes.
source: Neither the target sites for the highest expressed miRNA (miR-148-3p; CAGUGCA) nor any of the other circHIPK3-miRNAs are enriched among downregulated genes (p > 0.05, Chi-square test, Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C)
evidence: This is directly stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: An 11-mer motif AGGCCCCC(A/T)GC is present in the sequence of circHIPK3.
source: Aligning these nine 7-mers to circHIPK3 reveals a larger 11-mer within circHIPK3, AGGCCCCC(A/T)GC (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 2E.

claim: The 11-mer motif is enriched in downregulated genes compared to upregulated genes upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3.
source: Interestingly, the motif is enriched in downregulated genes compared to upregulated genes (p < 1e−39) and genes that are not differentially expressed (not DE) (p < 1e−28) in both UMUC3 (Chi-square test, Figure 2F)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The 11-mer motif is enriched in downregulated genes upon circHIPK3 KD in J82 cells.
source: and J82 cells (p < 0.0001 for both comparisons, Chi-square test, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Binding sites for GRWD1 (HepG2) and IGF2BP2 (K562) overlap the 11-mer motif in circHIPK3.
source: Specifically, binding sites for GRWD1 (HepG2) and IGF2BP2 (K562) overlap the 11-mer.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text based on eCLIP data analysis.

claim: circHIPK3 interacts with IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP2 as confirmed by RNA immunoprecipitation.
source: Using divergent primers targeting the unique backsplice junction of circHIPK3 (Supplementary file 1), we specifically verified circHIPK3 pull-down in IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP2 RIP experiments by semi-quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in both cell lines (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IGF2BP2-binding sites are enriched in genes that become downregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3, J82, and FL3.
source: Focusing on K562-RBPs, we found that while genes that become upregulated upon circHIPK3 KD generally contain more circHIPK3–RBP-binding sites (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), IGF2BP2-binding sites are enriched in genes that become downregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in both UMUC3, J82, and FL3 (all p < 0.05, Chi-square tests, Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: There is a significant overlap of altered genes between circHIPK3 KD in BC cell lines and IGF2BP2 KD in ENCODE experiments.
source: Therefore, we evaluated if genes affected by circHIPK3 KD in BC cell lines are also affected in ENCODE experiments of IGF2BP2 KD and found a significant overlap of altered genes (p < 2.2e−16, Fisher's exact tests, Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: Genes that are downregulated by circHIPK3 KD are primarily upregulated upon IGF2BP2 KD.
source: Interestingly, the genes that are downregulated by circHIPK3 KD are primarily upregulated upon IGF2BP2 KD suggesting an mRNA destabilization function of IGF2BP2 (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: circHIPK3 interacts strongly with IGF2BP2 in BC cells but not with GRWD1.
source: Consistent with our findings above, circHIPK3 interacts strongly with IGF2BP2 in BC cells but not with GRWD1 (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: IGF2BP2 interacts with ACTB mRNA with much lower affinity than with circHIPK3.
source: Importantly, IGF2BP2 interacts with ACTB mRNA with much lower affinity (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: Several proliferation pathways, including E2F targets and G2/M checkpoint, are upregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3 and J82 cells.
source: To assess the functional impact of circHIPK3 and IGF2BP2 in bladder carcinogenesis, we performed gene set enrichment analysis of 50 hallmarks of cancer gene sets (Liberzon et al., 2015) and found that several proliferation pathways, for example, E2F targets and G2/M checkpoint, are upregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in both UMUC3 (p < 0.05, T-test, Figure 4D) and J82 cells (p < 0.05, T-test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: Proliferation pathways are downregulated upon IGF2BP2 KD.
source: In contrast, these pathways are downregulated upon IGF2BP2 KD (p < 0.05, T-test, Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: STAT3 gene contains the 11-mer motif in its 3′UTR.
source: An interesting example is the STAT3 gene, which contains the 11-mer motif in its 3′UTR (allowing two mismatches)
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: STAT3 becomes downregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3.
source: becomes downregulated upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3 (P_24h = 3e−04, Wald test, Figure 5A)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: STAT3 is upregulated upon IGF2BP2 depletion in UMUC3 and J82 cells.
source: while it is upregulated upon IGF2BP2 depletion in both cell lines (p < 0.001, Wald test, Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: IGF2BP2 RIP experiments confirmed a STAT3–IGF2BP2 interaction in BC cells.
source: IGF2BP2 RIP experiments confirmed a STAT3–IGF2BP2 interaction in BC cells (p = 0.04, T-test, Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Upon immunoprecipitation of IGF2BP2, significantly more STAT3 mRNA binding is observed after circHIPK3 depletion.
source: Interestingly, upon immunoprecipitation of IGF2BP2, we observed significantly more STAT3 mRNA binding after circHIPK3 depletion (48 hr), supporting a regulatory role of circHIPK3 as a ceRNA (p < 0.007, T-test, Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: Binding of IGF2BP2 to circHIPK3 is reduced significantly when the 11-mer motif is scrambled.
source: Interestingly, we found that binding of IGF2BP2 was reduced significantly (~twofold, p = 0.028) when the 11-mer motif had been scrambled, while binding of STAT3 mRNA to IGF2BP2 was increased (~sevenfold, p = 0.036) (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: TP53 mRNA is upregulated upon circHIPK3 KD at later time points in UMUC3 cells.
source: Consistent with our predictions, TP53 mRNA is upregulated upon circHIPK3 KD at later time points in UMUC3 cells (p = 1.7e−05, Wald test, Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: circHIPK3 KD leads to downregulation of STAT3 protein and upregulation of p53 protein levels.
source: Additionally, western blot analysis confirmed that circHIPK3 KD indeed leads to downregulation of STAT3 protein, while p53 protein levels rise (p < 0.05, T-test, Figure 5H).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Nuclear and overall STAT3 protein levels are significantly lower upon circHIPK3 KD.
source: Finally, immunofluorescence staining showed that nuclear and overall STAT3 protein levels are significantly lower upon circHIPK3 KD (p < 0.003, Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test, Figure 5I)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Nuclear p53 protein levels are higher upon circHIPK3 KD.
source: while nuclear p53 protein levels are higher (p = 1.7e−30, Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test, Figure 5J).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 5J.

claim: circHIPK3 levels are approximately 45 (FL3), 51 (J82), and 40 (UMUC3) molecules per cell.
source: Isolating RNA from a known number of cells then allowed us to estimate the number of circHIPK3 molecules to ~45 (FL3), ~51 (J82), and ~40 (UMUC3) per cell (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: Each cell contains approximately 216,000 (FL3), 127,500 (J82), and 261,000 (UMUC3) IGF2BP2 molecules.
source: From known amounts of purified IGF2BP2 in western blots with lysates from a known number of BC cells, we estimate that each cell contains ~216,000 (FL3), ~127,500 (J82), and ~261,000 (UMUC3) IGF2BP2 molecules (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: IGF2BP2 significantly outnumbers circHIPK3 by several orders of magnitude.
source: These results suggest that IGF2BP2 significantly outnumbers circHIPK3 by several orders of magnitude and hence that a ceRNA function for circHIPK3, in its simplest form, is unlikely.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on quantification data.

claim: A significantly higher prevalence of large cytoplasmic condensates is observed in cells expressing high levels of circHIPK3 compared to controls (80% vs 29%).
source: Indeed, we observed a significantly higher prevalence of large cytoplasmic condensates in cells expressing high levels of circHIPK3 compared to controls (80% vs 29%) (Figure 6C, D)
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C, D.

claim: The expression of circHIPK3 is significantly upregulated in patients with NMIBC compared to patients with muscle invasive BC.
source: The expression of circHIPK3 is significantly upregulated in patients with NMIBC compared to patients with muscle invasive BC (p < 3.3e−09, Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test, Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: circHIPK3 levels are positively associated with overall survival in patients with NMIBC.
source: In a newly generated and hence independent cohort of patients with NMIBC (n = 56) (Strandgaard et al., 2022), we found that circHIPK3 levels are positively associated with overall survival (p < 0.009, Log-Rank Test, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: circHIPK3 is the most prevalent alpha circRNA.
source: CircHIPK3 (chr11:33307958–33309057) (hg19) is the most prevalent alpha circRNA, that is, it is the circRNA most often found to be highest expressed in human samples (Stagsted et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 originates from the second exon of the gene HIPK3.
source: It originates from the second exon of the gene HIPK3 and possesses highly conserved regions across species (Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 is expressed in patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) and correlates positively with BC progression independently of the parent gene.
source: In a previous study, we found that circHIPK3 is expressed in patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) and correlates positively with BC progression independently of the parent gene (Okholm et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 is higher expressed than the corresponding linear transcript.
source: Additionally, we found that circHIPK3 is higher expressed than the corresponding linear transcript and possesses key biological features, for example, enrichment of evolutionary conserved regions and miRNA target sites, indicating a regulatory function of its own.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on previous findings.

claim: STAT3 regulates TP53 expression by repressing its transcription.
source: It is well established that STAT3 regulates TP53 expression by repressing its transcription (Niu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: IGF2BP2 is generally an abundant ubiquitous protein with an estimated ~10,000 copies per cell in HeLa cells.
source: As IGF2BP2 is generally an abundant ubiquitous protein with an estimated ~10,000 copies per cell in HeLa cells (Bekker-Jensen et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circRNAs are endogenous predominantly non-coding RNAs, formed from precursor mRNA through backsplicing events.
source: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are endogenous predominantly non-coding RNAs, formed from precursor mRNA through backsplicing events (Starke et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: Recent improvements in next-generation sequencing of non-polyadenylated transcriptomes and bioinformatics technology have revealed the existence of thousands of human circRNAs.
source: Although first thought to be by-products or a result of erroneous splicing (Cocquerelle et al., 1993), recent improvements in next-generation sequencing of non-polyadenylated transcriptomes and bioinformatics technology have revealed the existence of thousands of human circRNAs (Jeck et al., 2013; Liu and Chen, 2022; Memczak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations.

claim: Many circRNAs can interact with RNA-binding proteins (RBPs).
source: Many circRNAs can interact with RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) (Ashwal-Fluss et al., 2014; Du et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations.

claim: Several circRNAs are suggested to function as miRNA sponges.
source: and several circRNAs are suggested to function as miRNA sponges (Li et al., 2015a; Li et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations.

claim: ciRS-7 and circSRY can bind a large number of miRNAs.
source: However, besides ciRS-7 and circSRY, which can bind a large number of miRNAs (Hansen et al., 2013; Memczak et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations.

claim: circRNAs are not enriched for more miRNA-binding sites than would be expected by chance.
source: circRNAs are not enriched for more miRNA-binding sites than would be expected by chance (Guo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: Some circRNAs can be translated into proteins under certain conditions.
source: Recently, it was discovered that some circRNAs can be translated into proteins under certain conditions (Chen et al., 2021; Petrucci et al., 2017; Pamudurti et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations.

claim: The majority of circRNAs likely do not encode proteins.
source: but the majority of circRNAs likely do not encode proteins (Stagsted et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: IGF2BP2 is a multifunctional RBP that affects hundreds of mRNAs and various RNA processes.
source: IGF2BP2 is a multifunctional RBP that affects hundreds of mRNAs and various RNA processes (Cao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: IGF2BP2 belongs to a family of three conserved RBPs (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3).
source: It belongs to a family of three conserved RBPs (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3), that are important modulators of gene expression, especially during development, and contain highly similar RNA-binding domains; two N-terminal RNA-recognition motifs and four C-terminal hnRNPK Homology (KH) domains (reviewed in Bell et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: A consensus binding motif for IGF2BP2 is CUCAC-(N10-15)-(A/U)-GG-(A/U), containing the core elements CA and GG required for specific binding of the IGF2BP2 KH3 and KH4 domain.
source: Recently, Biswas identified a consensus binding motif for IGF2BP2, CUCAC-(N10-15)-(A/U)-GG-(A/U), containing the core elements CA and GG required for specific binding of the IGF2BP2 KH3 and KH4 domain, respectively (Biswas et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: IGF2BP2 is overexpressed in many cancers, correlates with progression, and promotes cancer cell proliferation and migration.
source: Studies have shown that IGF2BP2 is overexpressed in many cancers, correlates with progression, and promotes cancer cell proliferation and migration (reviewed in Cao et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 is downregulated in BC.
source: while we and others have reported that circHIPK3 is downregulated in BC (Okholm et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 possesses tumor suppressor functions.
source: and possess tumor suppressor functions (Teng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: circHIPK3 functions as a ceRNA for IGF2BP2 by specifically interacting with IGF2BP2 at the 11-mer-binding site.
source: Our experiments suggest that circHIPK3 functions as a ceRNA for IGF2BP2 most likely by specifically interacting with IGF2BP2 at the 11-mer-binding site (and potentially secondary sites), which affects IGF2BP2-binding affinity to other target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on experimental results.

claim: circHIPK3 represses STAT3 expression while upregulating p53.
source: This in turn represses STAT3 expression while upregulating p53.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on experimental results.

claim: Even a few circHIPK3 molecules can function as ceRNAs by nucleating numerous IGF2BP2 molecules per circRNA.
source: Since ectopic expression of circHIPK3 induces IGF2BP2 condensation within cells, we propose that even a few circHIPK3 molecules can function as a ceRNAs by nucleating numerous IGF2BP2 molecules per circRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on experimental observations and interpretation.

claim: The expression of circHIPK3 is positively associated with overall survival in BC patients.
source: Finally, by analyzing large patient cohorts with rich clinical annotations, we show that the expression of circHIPK3 is positively associated with overall survival in BC patients.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on patient cohort analysis.

claim: circHIPK3 nucleates IGF2BP2 and functions as a competing endogenous RNA.
source: circHIPK3 nucleates IGF2BP2 and functions as a competing endogenous RNA
evidence: This is the title of the manuscript, summarizing the main findings.

claim: circHIPK3 can sequester IGF2BP2 as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA), leading to target mRNA stabilization.
source: Our results suggest that circHIPK3 can sequester IGF2BP2 as a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA), leading to target mRNA stabilization.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract summarizing the findings.

claim: Manipulation of circHIPK3 regulates IGF2BP2-STAT3 mRNA binding and, thereby, STAT3 mRNA levels.
source: As an example of a circHIPK3-regulated gene, we focus on the STAT3 mRNA as a specific substrate of IGF2BP2 and validate that manipulation of circHIPK3 regulates IGF2BP2-STAT3 mRNA binding and, thereby, STAT3 mRNA levels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract summarizing the findings.

claim: Absolute copy number quantifications demonstrate that IGF2BP2 outnumbers circHIPK3 by orders of magnitude.
source: Surprisingly, absolute copy number quantifications demonstrate that IGF2BP2 outnumbers circHIPK3 by orders of magnitude, which is inconsistent with a simple 1:1 ceRNA hypothesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract summarizing the findings.

claim: circHIPK3 can nucleate multiple copies of IGF2BP2, potentially via phase separation, to produce IGF2BP2 condensates.
source: Instead, we show that circHIPK3 can nucleate multiple copies of IGF2BP2, potentially via phase separation, to produce IGF2BP2 condensates.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract summarizing the findings.

claim: A few cellular circHIPK3 molecules can induce IGF2BP2 condensation, thereby regulating key factors for cell proliferation.
source: Our results support a model where a few cellular circHIPK3 molecules can induce IGF2BP2 condensation, thereby regulating key factors for cell proliferation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract summarizing the findings.

claim: circHIPK3 is highly expressed in the cytoplasm of HepG2 and K562 cells.
source: We analyzed circHIPK3 localization in total RNA-Seq datasets of fractionated cells (The ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012) and found that circHIPK3 is highly expressed in the cytoplasm of HepG2 and K562 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to data and a citation.

claim: All circHIPK3–RBPs occupy the cytoplasmic fraction of the cell, except for U2AF1 and U2AF2.
source: From immunofluorescence imaging of RBP localization in HepG2 (Van Nostrand et al., 2020), we found that all circHIPK3–RBPs occupy the cytoplasmic fraction of the cell, except for U2AF1 and U2AF2, which span the intron–exon boundary at 3′ splice sites and are instrumental for mRNA splicing (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: The 11-mer motif and IGF2BP2-binding sites are highly enriched in upregulated genes upon IGF2BP2 KD.
source: Accordingly, the 11-mer motif and IGF2BP2-binding sites are highly enriched in upregulated genes (p < 6e−19, Chi-square test, Figure 3H, I).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in figures.

claim: There is a significant overlap between genes containing the 11-mer motif and the IGF2BP2 KH34 RE in their 3′UTRs.
source: Here, we found a significant overlap between genes containing the 11-mer motif and the IGF2BP2 KH34 RE in their 3′UTRs (p < 2.2e−16, Fisher's exact test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in a figure.

claim: The IGF2BP2 KH34 RE is enriched in downregulated genes upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3 cells.
source: Additionally, the IGF2BP2 KH34 RE is enriched in downregulated genes upon circHIPK3 KD in UMUC3 cells (p < 0.002, Chi-square test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in a figure.

claim: There is no difference in IGF2BP2 gene expression between circHIPK3 KD and scr samples in UMUC3.
source: We observed no difference in IGF2BP2 gene expression between circHIPK3 KD and scr samples in UMUC3 (p = 0.41, likelihood ratio test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in a figure.

claim: There is a slight, though significant, difference in IGF2BP2 gene expression at later time points in J82 cells upon circHIPK3 KD.
source: and only a slight, though significant, difference at later time points in J82 cells (p = 0.003, likelihood ratio test, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is stated with statistical support and shown in a figure.

claim: IGF2BP2-binding affinity to STAT3 is 2.9 times higher in the presence of the 11-mer ASO compared to control samples.
source: Although not statistically significant, IGF2BP2-binding affinity to STAT3 is 2.9 times higher in the presence of the 11-mer ASO compared to control samples (p = 0.078, T-test, Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical information and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The relative circHIPK3–IGF2BP2-binding affinity is 30% lower in 11-mer ASO samples.
source: Additionally, the relative circHIPK3–IGF2BP2-binding affinity is 30% lower in 11-mer ASO samples (p = 0.27, T-test, Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical information and shown in a figure.

claim: Cells expressed similar levels of RNase R-resistant WT and mutant circHIPK3.
source: Importantly, cells expressed similar levels of RNase R-resistant WT and mutant circHIPK3 as judged by northern blotting (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in a figure.

claim: circHIPK3 was produced in ~fourfold excess of the linear precursor.
source: and circHIPK3 was produced in ~fourfold excess of the linear precursor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in a figure.

claim: Double KD of circHIPK3 and IGF2BP2 restored target mRNA expression in J82 cells.
source: In support of our ceRNA model, the single KDs confirmed the previously observed expression pattern (down- and upregulation for circHIPK3 and IGF2BP2, respectively), while double KD indeed restored target mRNA expression in J82 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in a figure.

claim: circHIPK3 may recruit unknown enzymatic modifiers of IGF2BP2, which in turn could affect its activity.
source: Alternatively, circHIPK3 may recruit unknown enzymatic modifiers of IGF2BP2, which in turn could affect its activity.
evidence: This is stated as an alternative hypothesis in the text.

claim: Both scenarios (nucleation and enzymatic modification) could explain the functional output from a small number of circHIPK3 molecules in cells.
source: Both scenarios could explain the functional output from a small number of circHIPK3 molecules in cells and await further experimentation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the text.

claim: Most reports claiming circRNA-specific miRNA sponging are based on inflated circRNA expression, use of miRNA mimics and reporter assays.
source: In addition, since most reports claiming circRNA-specific miRNA sponging are based on inflated circRNA expression, use of miRNA mimics and reporter assays, a conclusion that circRNAs are generally functioning as miRNA sponges should be taken with some caution.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a critical evaluation of the literature.

claim: Less than a hundred circHIPK3 molecules per cell questions the miRNA-sponge hypothesis.
source: Indeed, our estimation of less than a hundred circHIPK3 molecules per cell, questions the miRNA-sponge hypothesis, as this entails specific sequence-specific binding of miRNA-guided Argonaute proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on quantification data.

claim: Several studies argue against a general miRNA-sponge function for most circRNAs.
source: Nonetheless, several studies argue against a general miRNA-sponge function for most circRNAs (Guo et al., 2014; Militello et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: RNA structure could explain the discrepancies observed in IGF2BP2 binding motifs.
source: While some RBPs contain well-established binding domains and bind to well-defined motifs, most RBPs rely on sequence context and structural features (Dominguez et al., 2018; Doyle and Kiebler, 2012), suggesting that RNA structure could explain the discrepancies observed here.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: IGF2BP2 might recognize the swapped orientation of the REs, as observed for IGF2BP1.
source: Additionally, IGF2BP2 might recognize the swapped orientation of the REs, as observed for IGF2BP1 (Patel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Additional RNA-binding domains are involved in RNA recognition and distinction between targets for IGF2BPs.
source: Although earlier work has shown that the KH34 domains are the major RNA-binding domains of all IGF2BPs (Chao et al., 2010; Patel et al., 2012), more recent studies demonstrate that additional RNA-binding domains are involved in RNA recognition and distinction between targets (Schneider et al., 2019; Wächter et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: External factors likely influence binding affinity and preference of IGF2BPs, and cooperativity both intra- and intermolecularly might be restricted to certain cells, tissues, and environment.
source: Furthermore, other external factors likely influence binding affinity and preference, and cooperativity both intra- and intermolecularly might be restricted to certain cells, tissues, and environment, as observed for circFoxo3, which interacts with different RBPs depending on the biological setting (Du et al., 2017b; Du et al., 2017a; Du et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: STAT3 is persistently activated in a wide diversity of cancers and is positively associated with cell proliferation, cell survival, invasion, and metastasis.
source: STAT3 is persistently activated in a wide diversity of cancers and is positively associated with cell proliferation, cell survival, invasion, and metastasis (reviewed in Kamran et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: Tumor suppressor activities under certain conditions, and in certain cancers, have also been reported for STAT3.
source: although tumor suppressor activities under certain conditions, and in certain cancers, have also been reported for STAT3 (reviewed in Tolomeo and Cascio, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation.

claim: A study recently used an mRNA–RBP tethering reporter assay and found a general mRNA destabilizing effect of an IGF2BP2–mRNA association.
